movie.title: Primate
movie.overview: College student Lucy and her friends spend their vacation at her family's home in Hawaii, which includes her pet chimpanzee, Ben. However, when Ben contracts rabies after being bitten by a rabid animal, the group must fight for their lives in order to avoid the now-violent chimp.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: It’s been a while since “Lucy” (Johnny Sequoyah) has been home to her luxury family home in Hawai’i, so her arrival with friend “Kate” (Victoria Wyant) and the not quite so welcome “Hannah” (Jess Alexander) is eagerly awaited by her deaf dad “Adam” (Troy Kotsur), her younger sister “Erin” (Gia Hunter) and the undoubted star of the film - their pet chimp “Ben”. Now any sense of jeopardy which we might have had coming into this fearsome frat-flesh-fest is somewhat negated by the fact that there is a very useful slide at the top of the film that explains to us the dangers of hydrophobia. Putting two and two together does not require Stephen Hawking and so what we watch for the next ninety minutes sees a lot of people go ape. As ever with these type of films, I found myself largely disinterested in the characterisations of the humans - they are all the usual unremarkable people who’d readily bore you to death at a party, so with the exception of the mostly absent author “Adam” who did bring a little charisma to the proceedings, they were entirely deserving of their grizzly fates - especially the three hormonal boys whose short shrift did raise a smile, I have to admit. The plot is full of holes and some of the dialogue is really banal, but in best Rudd Weatherwax tradition it’s the animal that out-acts everyone and had me rooting for him. The moral? Well perhaps that’s just never to mix a mongoose and a chimpanzee?

reviews.author: Enes
reviews.content: I thought it was a good film. The monkey seemed to have rabies and a personality disorder. The 2-hour film flowed very well; I wasn't bored. The camera zoomed in nicely on the violent scenes. It made me nauseous. The acting was passable, the effects were good, and the script was very similar to another film I've seen, but I can't remember the name. Is it worth watching? Give it a chance. It gets a 7 out of 10. Thanks for your efforts. Enjoy the movie!

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content:
If your ape fails in your apemovie... run
If you are hinging your entire premise on that the ape is supposed to be central, and scary, like a Chucky or a M3gan or a Shakma, then you need to make it look really good. And this one does not. Its face is not expressive enough, and you can only hide so much of the clunky motions by making the movie dark. The characters are nice, the story is what it needs to be, but the ape lets all of this down.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: A tropical vacation turns into a desperate fight for survival when a college student's beloved pet chimpanzee contracts rabies and brutally turns on her group of friends.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: College student Lucy travels to her family's home in Hawaii alongside her close friends for a relaxing getaway, accompanied by her domesticated pet chimpanzee, Ben. The idyllic vacation quickly devolves into horror when Ben is bitten by a rabid creature and contracts the deadly infection. As the virus takes hold, the once-gentle ape turns unpredictably violent, forcing the stranded group to fight for their lives against an apex predator they once considered family.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Lucy, a college student, decides to host a tropical getaway for her friends at her family's remote estate in Hawaii. Joining the trip is Ben, Lucy's domesticated pet chimpanzee, who has shared a deep emotional bond with her since childhood. The vacation starts off on a cheerful note, filled with sun, relaxation, and fond bonding moments among the group. However, the atmosphere shifts dramatically after Ben strays into the surrounding wilderness and gets bitten by an infected wild animal. Unbeknownst to the group, the bite transmits the rabies virus, which begins to rapidly alter the chimp's neurological state. Ben's behavior grows increasingly erratic, escalating from mild agitation to outbursts of unprovoked aggression. The situation reaches a deadly climax when the virus fully takes over, transforming the powerful primate into a relentless, territorial killer. Trapped in the isolated compound without immediate help, Lucy and her friends must navigate both physical horror and psychological anguish. Lucy is forced to confront the tragic reality that her beloved pet is gone, and the survivors must unite to outsmart a dangerously intelligent predator before they are hunted down one by one.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Set against the lush, sun-soaked backdrop of Hawaii, Primate explores the terrifying collapse of trust between humans and nature. When college student Lucy returns to her family's Hawaiian home for a summer break with her friends, the main highlight is Ben—a smart, lovable pet chimpanzee she raised from a young age. The secluded estate offers a perfect paradise, but unseen dangers lurk in the surrounding tropical jungle. When Ben suffers an animal bite, an insidious rabies infection quickly takes root, altering his brain chemistry and stripping away his domesticated nature. As night falls and the infection reaches its peak, the once-tender bond between Lucy and Ben is shattered, leaving the group isolated and fighting for survival against an agile, immensely strong, and enraged creature. Blending intense creature-feature horror with psychological drama, the story crafts a tense, high-stakes battle for survival in paradise.
